html:
The Kurâ, better known as the Bakairi, are a Cariban-speaking people of central Mato Grosso, Brazil, on the upper Paranatinga and Teles Pires rivers at the southern edge of the Xingu basin. Kurâ is their own name for themselves.

One branch lived on the upper Xingu among peoples such as the Kalapalo, and another to the west. In 1884 Bakairi guides took the German explorer Karl von den Steinen down the Xingu, the first scientific expedition there, which made them well known in Europe. In the 1900s the Brazilian state gathered the Bakairi at government posts, and today they live mainly on two indigenous lands in Mato Grosso. Their language is one of the Cariban languages of Brazil.
